item.title: 31 Years Later, Calvin and Hobbes' Scariest Comic Is Still a Controversial Classic
item.description: On a Halloween reread of Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes , one of its more remarkable qualities is that it usually doesn't bother with that. There are a few seasonal strips and arcs scattered across its nine-year run, sure, and Calvin's struggle with staying good before Christmas is an annual tradition. But as a whole, C&H is less concerned with the holiday calendar than one might expect, particularly in its late, post- sabbatical era.

item.title: Pokémon Officially Returns to Galar in 2027 for New Release
item.description: Disney and Pokémon are teaming up for a new streaming series coming to Disney Plus in 2027. Disney and The Pokémon Company announced Friday that the stop-motion animated adventure series Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd & Pichu is now slated to debut on Disney XD and to stream exclusively on Disney Plus in 2027.

item.title: 10 NES Games That Are Still Worth Playing From Start to Finish
item.description: On Oct. 18, 1985, Nintendo released the Nintendo Entertainment System in North America alongside a limited selection of games like Super Mario Bros. and Excitebike . Within a few years, it had a library of hundreds of titles, proving that rumors of the video game industry’s death throughout the early ‘80s were greatly exaggerated. Today, many of those early games feel like antiques. They’re not nearly as memorable as they once were, with so many generations of newer software to choose from. But there are some that still deserve your attention, even now. Here are 10 NES games that are still worth playing from start to finish.

item.title: 9 Best DLCs That Were Even Better Than the Base Game
item.description: Even the wildest DLC needs a solid game to swerve away from, or the swerve doesn’t land. Every base game with excellent DLC is strong enough to stand on its own. That’s the common DNA: studios that had built something sturdy enough to trust it, confident enough to hand players a portal to hell, an alien hive-mind under a suburban cul-de-sac, or a crown that makes you ruler of an entire realm of madness — and bet that players would play anyway. For these nine DLCs, that confidence turned out to be well-placed. Here are the best DLCs of all time that took their main story and had the confidence to dream up wild new experiences for dedicated players. Each of these nine game expansions took a big swing, and has been remembered for that creativity ever since.

item.title: Resident Evil Director Is Already Thinking Sequels
item.description: Weapons director Zach Cregger took a very different approach with his new adaptation of Resident Evil . Rather than adapting the characters and narrative of Capcom's survival-horror game franchise, Cregger is instead translating what it feels like to exist in one of Resident Evil 's worst-case scenarios. Resident Evil follows a hapless medical courier, played by Austin Abrams, as he attempts to survive a journey to Raccoon City, which is now infested with zombies and other monstrosities.

item.title: Adam Scott's Criminally Overlooked 2026 Thriller Is Finally on Streaming
item.description: You know it's been a good year for horror movies when a genuine hit still slips through the cracks. We spent the summer on discourse over Obsession, The Backrooms , Zach Cregger's Resident Evil , and The End of Oak Street , all of which pulled in nine-digit takes at the box office. Before that, 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple was a critical if not a commercial success. Usually horror fans have to sort through indies for their genre fix, but this year has been a movable feast.

item.title: 63 Years Later, the Stellar Action Comic Strip Most America Never Heard of Deserves Another Shot
item.description: This goes double for newspaper comics, which are often viewed as disposable in ways that graphic novels aren't. Surprisingly few of them ever pick up an international audience. Exceptions include Andy Capp and Fred Basset , British strips that have substantially outlived their original creators. They do not include the British Dennis the Menace , which debuted in Beano in 1951, five days after Hank Ketcham started a strip by the same name in America.

item.title: New Steam Game is Basically Kiki’s Delivery Service in Video Game Form
item.description: Sharing food with others begets a certain type of magic. That goes double for baked goods and desserts. In The Witch’s Bakery , that magic is literal. It’s a charming, cozy, and heartfelt adventure that goes heavy on the Studio Ghibli vibes.
